feed.title: Ford accused of hiding a keyless entry theft risk in new class action lawsuit
feed.summary: A new class action lawsuit has been filed against Ford Motor Co., alleging that the company knowingly sold vehicles equipped with a "Smart Key" passive keyless entry system that is easily defeated by thieves. The lawsuit claims Ford has been aware of this vulnerability since 2011 but failed to disclose it to buyers, leading to increased theft risks and decreased resale values for affected models like the F-150, Bronco, Explorer, Mustang, and Escape. The plaintiff seeks triple damages, a disgorgement of profits, attorney's fees, and an order for Ford to inform current owners about the security flaw.

feed.title: Target names Weinstein chief marketing, guest experience officer
feed.summary: Target has appointed Mark Weinstein as chief marketing and guest experience officer to enhance consumer connections and drive growth. Weinstein, formerly Hilton's global CMO, will oversee brand engagement, Roundel, and Target+, reporting directly to CEO Michael Fiddelke. His role involves shaping a connected customer experience across all touchpoints as Target focuses on strengthening its brand and guest experience.

feed.title: Altria Group (NYSE:MO) Shares Up 2.5% After Insider Buying Activity
feed.summary: Altria Group (NYSE:MO) shares rose 2.5% after director Kathryn McQuade purchased 1,500 shares for $101,430, increasing her stake by 1.32%. The company recently increased its quarterly dividend to $1.11 per share, resulting in a 6.3% yield, though its latest adjusted EPS narrowly missed analyst estimates. Analysts maintain a mixed view, with a consensus "Hold" rating and an average price target of $70.11.

feed.title: Costco just might have a future in Asheville
feed.summary: Costco has resubmitted plans to build a 166,000-square-foot facility in Asheville's Enka Commerce Park, including a 32-pump gas station and 914 parking spaces. This comes after the retailer withdrew its initial application earlier in the year due to complications with scope, timeline, and costs. The new proposal addresses previous concerns regarding road changes, stormwater infrastructure on a former industrial site, and traffic impact, and will now go before the city's Planning & Zoning Commission and City Council for approval.

feed.title: Netflix stock jumps as Wall Street sees a new growth engine
feed.summary: Netflix stock rose by about 3% after Evercore increased its price target, highlighting live events as a significant new growth opportunity. Analyst Kutgun Maral raised the target to $110 from $100, maintaining an outperform rating, noting that 45% of new subscribers in Japan joined due to a World Baseball Classic promotion. Evercore also sees potential in shorter content, with 38% of U.S. respondents using Netflix Clips, suggesting diversification beyond traditional series and films.

feed.title: Adobe (ADBE): A Billion Users, But Wall Street Wants Proof It Pays
feed.summary: Adobe Inc. reported Q3 fiscal 2026 results with revenue of $6.76 billion, exceeding analyst expectations, and non-GAAP EPS of $6.13. Despite reaching one billion monthly active users and significant AI-first ARR growth, the company's shares fell due to Q4 revenue guidance slightly below consensus and a 38% year-over-year decline in net new ARR. Analysts are divided, with some maintaining Outperform ratings due to user growth and AI momentum, while others express concern over the slowing ARR growth and the need for a strong Q4 to validate future growth.

feed.title: Kraft Heinz CEO: ‘We’ve got an issue in Oscar Mayer’
feed.summary: Kraft Heinz CEO Steven Cahillane acknowledged significant issues with its Oscar Mayer brand, particularly with Deli Fresh lunch meat packaging leading to share losses. The company is rolling out redesigned packaging and increasing investment in marketing, sales, R&D, and product improvements to revive the brand and align it with consumer trends toward healthier options.

feed.title: Adyen N.V. Joins Guidewire Software, Inc. Marketplace As An Approved Global Payment Partner For Insurers
feed.summary: Adyen N.V. has been approved as a Global Payment Partner for Guidewire Software, Inc., integrating its payment capabilities into the Guidewire Marketplace for property and casualty insurers. This integration aims to provide a single global platform for managing the entire flow of funds throughout the policy lifecycle, eliminating fragmented regional setups. Key features include end-to-end processing, unified reporting, built-in fraud protection, and advanced data security, with global availability planned for 2027.

feed.title: Lilly says Foundayo has captured over 30% of new US patients on oral weight-loss drugs
feed.summary: Eli Lilly announced that its oral obesity treatment, Foundayo, has secured over 30% of new patients in the U.S. market, significantly closing the gap on Novo Nordisk's Wegovy pill. The demand for oral weight-loss drugs is growing as they appeal to patients who prefer not to use injections and help alleviate supply issues associated with injectable therapies, with the overall obesity treatment market expected to exceed $100 billion annually in the U.S. by 2030. Lilly's injectable Zepbound is also performing well in the U.S. Medicare program, while the company navigates new generic competition in international markets.

feed.title: EviCore expands coverage for Guardant’s Shield cancer test
feed.summary: EviCore, a subsidiary of Cigna and the second-largest specialty benefits manager in the U.S., will expand coverage for Guardant Health Inc.'s Shield blood test for colorectal cancer screening starting January 1, 2027. This expansion increases the total covered lives for Shield to approximately 94 million, applying to individuals aged 45 and older at average risk for colorectal cancer. Guardant's Shield test is FDA-approved, included in major cancer guidelines, and has been performed over 200,000 times in real-world settings.

Other major Wall Street banks like Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley also saw their shares decline. feed.title: Paramount Skydance (NASDAQ:PSKY) Stock Gains After Pulling Out of Netflix Agreement

While the specific Skydance Animation deal has ended due to the integration of Skydance Animation into Paramount, both companies stated they would continue their broader content licensing relationship and release existing co-productions. Meanwhile, a separate report warned that Paramount's departure from California could cause $1.01 billion to $2.03 billion in economic damage to the state.

feed.title: AI infrastructure company Cornelis raises $205M to chip away at Nvidia’s dominance
feed.summary: Cornelis, an AI infrastructure company, has raised $205 million in funding led by IAG Capital Partners. The company, which spun off from Intel in 2020, aims to challenge Nvidia's dominance by developing networking technology that allows AI chips to communicate more efficiently. Their new product, Active Compute Fabric, addresses the issue of wasted GPU time by enabling simultaneous processing and data transmission, offering an open architecture compatible with various GPU and accelerator hardware.

feed.title: Trump administration announces $16 million for mining education at Kings Mountain lithium site
feed.summary: The Trump administration has announced a $16 million program to boost mining education in the U.S., specifically at the Kings Mountain lithium site. This initiative aims to address the significant disparity in mining engineer graduates between the U.S. and China, with the U.S. currently graduating far fewer. The funding will support the 14 accredited mining schools nationwide, with Virginia Tech being the closest to the Kings Mountain location.

feed.title: Wells Fargo commercial banking head Manning to retire, Biodrowski to succeed
feed.summary: John Manning, Wells Fargo's executive vice president and head of commercial banking market coverage, is set to retire at the end of 2026 after over 30 years with the bank. Rob Biodrowski, currently a division executive for the U.S. Midwest commercial banking, will succeed Manning starting in November. Biodrowski will lead more than 2,000 bankers serving clients across the U.S. and Canada, focusing on companies with annual revenues from $25 million to $2 billion.

feed.title: Netflix Stock Rose 4% While the AI Trade Sold Off on Monday. Its Capital Goes Into Shows, Not Silicon.
feed.summary: Netflix stock rose 4% on Monday while AI-related stocks experienced a sell-off, driven by investor concerns about the high costs associated with AI development. Unlike AI companies, Netflix's significant capital expenditures are directed towards content creation rather than silicon and data centers. The streaming giant's strong free cash flow and stock repurchase program further highlight its financial health, though slowing revenue growth remains a key concern for its long-term stock performance.

feed.title: Deere recalls 375 workers to boost inventory ahead of contract talks
feed.summary: John Deere is rehiring 375 workers in the Quad Cities to build inventory in anticipation of upcoming labor negotiations, following the United Auto Workers' rejection of a contract extension due to job security concerns. This move comes after Deere laid off over 2,000 workers since April 2024 amidst an agricultural downturn. The company aims to ensure uninterrupted customer service and equipment access during future talks with the UAW.

feed.title: Working to Avoid Strike, Boeing Advances Another SPEEA Offer
feed.summary: Boeing is highly motivated to avoid a strike by its white-collar engineers and technicians, represented by SPEEA, as a labor disruption could hinder 737 MAX production and certification progress for the MAX 10 and 777X. The company has presented a new "final offer" to SPEEA, including a 10% guaranteed wage increase and annual wage pools. Meanwhile, machinists in Wichita, formerly with Spirit AeroSystems, have voted to rejoin the main IAM union contract, seeking equal footing with their Pacific Northwest counterparts.

feed.title: Worker killed in incident at Global Industrial facility identified
feed.summary: A 56-year-old worker, Ernest Appau, died on September 9 after being pinned between a loading ramp and a truck at a Global Industrial warehouse in Buford, Gwinnett County. Emergency responders were unable to revive him at the scene, and police found no signs of foul play after reviewing security footage. Company officials extended their condolences and stated that the incident remains under investigation to determine the cause.

feed.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman, LLC Announces an Investigation Against Baidu, Inc. (BIDU) and Encourages Shareholders to Learn More About the Investigation
feed.summary: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman, LLC has launched an investigation into potential claims against Baidu, Inc. (BIDU) following several significant drops in its American Depositary Share (ADS) price. These declines occurred after reports of Baidu being added to a list of companies aiding the Chinese military, and subsequent financial results showing year-over-year revenue decreases and increased competition in its advertising business. The firm encourages shareholders to participate in the investigation regarding their losses.
